question: What is the primary role of nurses in health care waste management?
explanation: Nurses manage patient care areas and initiate waste handling right where it is generated. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: Why is proper health care waste management critical for the community?

options.A: It reduces the overall cost of hospital construction
options.B: It guarantees faster recovery times for patients
options.C: It eliminates the need for municipal water treatment
options.D: It prevents toxic exposure and disease spread

explanation: Unmanaged clinical waste can release harmful pathogens and toxins into the public environment. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: Used scalpel blades and hypodermic needles fall under which waste category?
explanation: Any item capable of cutting or puncturing the skin is classified as sharps waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: Expired paracetamol syrups and leftover antibiotics should be classified as what type of waste?
explanation: Expired or unused medications belong to the pharmaceutical waste stream to prevent environmental contamination. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: What is the main goal of the waste minimization step?

options.C: Reducing the volume of waste produced

explanation: Minimization aims to decrease the total amount of waste generated at the source. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: How can a nurse actively help minimize health care waste?

options.A: By burying extra bandages behind the ward
options.B: By washing and reusing disposable syringes
options.C: By combining clinical bins to save space
options.D: By avoiding the over-opening of sterile supplies

explanation: Careful use of clinical materials prevents unnecessary generation of medical refuse. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: When must waste segregation take place in a clinical setting?

options.A: During the final municipal sorting stage
options.B: At the end of every nursing shift
options.C: Only after transport to the incinerator
options.D: Immediately at the point of origin

explanation: Waste must be sorted right where it is generated to prevent hazardous cross-contamination. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h4)

question: What is the consequence of throwing a used syringe into a general waste bin?

options.A: It contaminates safe waste and risks injury
options.B: It reduces the cost of municipal disposal
options.D: It converts hazardous waste into paper

explanation: Mixing hazardous sharps into general waste endangers sanitation workers and ruins the non-hazardous batch. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h4)

question: At what capacity should a clinical waste bag be tied and removed?
explanation: Bags are closed at three-quarters capacity to allow safe tying and prevent ruptures. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h5)

question: Why is pressing down on a full waste bag with your hands dangerous?

options.A: It slows down the municipal collection truck
options.B: It risks puncture injuries from hidden sharps
options.C: It increases the chemical toxicity of the air

explanation: Compacting bags manually exposes workers to accidental punctures from improperly disposed needles. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h5)

question: Where should a temporary health care waste storage room be located?

options.A: Away from food and patient areas
options.B: At the main hospital entrance porch

explanation: Waste storage must be isolated to prevent cross-contamination and unpleasant odors near sensitive zones. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h6)

question: What feature is NOT required in a proper medical waste storage facility?
explanation: Carpets trap moisture, pathogens, and fluids, making them unsuitable for medical waste rooms. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h6)

question: Which method uses pressurized steam to sterilize infectious medical waste?
explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure steam to destroy microorganisms before waste goes to a landfill. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: What must happen to hazardous medical waste before it is sent to a standard municipal landfill?

options.A: It needs to be compressed into smaller blocks
options.B: It should be mixed with large amounts of water
options.C: It must be wrapped in transparent polythene
options.D: It must undergo proper treatment to neutralize hazards

explanation: Treatment ensures that pathogens and toxins are destroyed before the waste reaches common disposal sites. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: Which vaccination is mandatory for healthcare workers handling clinical waste?
explanation: Hepatitis B immunization protects staff against bloodborne pathogen transmission from contaminated sharps. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h8)

question: What is the first action a nurse should take after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Soak the affected finger in strong bleach
options.B: Wash the site immediately with soap and water
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.D: Apply a tight bandage to stop blood circulation

explanation: Immediate washing reduces viral load at the wound site before reporting and seeking prophylaxis. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h8)
